c: Use 82–84% fat dry (tourage) butter; sheet at 10–12 °C to 19 × 19 cm per 500 g; dough and butter same firmness (finger test) at lock-in.
Détrempe DDT 24 °C; retard 12 h (flavour, relaxed gluten); butter 25–30% of dough weight (croissant), 30–35% (Danish), 40% (puff).
1 double (×4) + 1 single (×3) = 12 butter layers (open honeycomb, modern); 3 singles = 27 (classic, finer); avoid > 81 (layers fuse).
Chill 20–30 min between folds; brush off flour; seal edges; rotate 90° every fold.
Sheeter steps max 5 mm reduction per pass at the end; final 3.5–4 mm croissant, 4 mm Danish.
Proof 26–27 °C, RH 75%, 2–2.5 h until wobbly with visible layers; never > 28 °C (butter leaks).
Leaking butter = over-warm proof/under-proof; tight dense crumb = under-proof; no honeycomb = butter broke (too cold) or merged (too warm).
Egg-wash twice (start and end of proof); bake 175–180 °C convection 16–18 min to deep amber.
Assume 1.4 pieces per cover: 280 pieces = 120 croissants, 60 pain au chocolat, 50 Danish, 50 rolls/brioche.
Dough: 3 × 2.1 kg croissant batches + 1 Danish batch; shape the day before, retard at 4 °C on racks covered.
04:00 racks into proofer 27 °C 75% RH · 06:00 egg-wash · 06:15 bake in 3 waves (06:15, 07:15, 08:30) to keep the display fresh.
Display max 2 h; refill from the next wave; day-old to almond croissants or bread pudding (record waste each morning).
Allergen labels on every basket: gluten, milk, eggs, nuts where filled.
